vulns.title: create_protocol accepts any drop witness without a one-time-witness check, so a forged witness mints a privileged AdminCap that drains the shared vault
vulns.root_cause: create_protocol is `public` and generic over `<T: drop>`, taking the witness by value (`_witness: T`) but never restricting who may call it; it mints and returns a privileged `AdminCap`. So an attacker declares a throwaway `struct A has drop {}`, grabs the `Coin<FEE>` that `init` shares publicly plus a `coin::zero<EUR>()`, and calls `create_protocol(A {}, fee, coin::zero<EUR>(), ctx)` to receive a fresh `AdminCap` even though `init` already created the protocol once. Because `change_interest<T>(_, _cap: &AdminCap, _)` accepts any `&AdminCap` (the cap is not bound to a specific `Protocol`), the forged cap works on the real shared `Protocol<FEE>`: the attacker sets `interest_bp` to 0 so `borrow` accrues zero debt, `check_invariant` (`debt <= collateral * 7000 / 10000`) passes with no collateral, and the attacker drains the shared loan vault. Note that asserting `sui::types::is_one_time_witness(&witness)` does NOT fix this: `FEE` is an ordinary `drop` struct (the module's genuine one-time witness would be `DEEP_POCKETS`), and `init` itself calls `create_protocol(FEE {}, …)`, so the assert would abort `init`. The correct fix is to remove `public` from `create_protocol` so only this module's `init` can mint the `AdminCap`, making protocol creation a genuine once-at-init privilege; equivalently, restructure the module to receive its real one-time witness `DEEP_POCKETS` in `init` and assert `is_one_time_witness` on that.
